briefs.findings: The owner-approved vision serves one reader saving articles and marking them read, preserving titles and addresses. Accounts, sharing and recommendations are excluded. Design chooses local Node and JSON persistence, a queue owning save/list/mark-read, and presentation using only public queue operations. The glossary includes read articles in the queue. All documents explicitly settle intent and design; no interview is needed.
limitations: No README, instructions, standards, decisions, audit record or planned-change documents were found.

briefs.findings: Documented responsibilities distinguish queue state from presentation and storage. The tracked and working-tree file inventory contains only three documents; runtime interfaces and data flow cannot be observed. Implementation readiness is inferred to be pre-implementation, not a demonstrated application failure. Measurement over the two-commit history found one design/glossary co-change; this is advisory and gives no basis for restructuring.
limitations: No code or dependency graph exists to analyze. No two declared plans exist for overlap analysis.

briefs.findings: No manifest, native check command, test, CI or entry point exists. The approved save/list/mark-read journey and JSON persistence have no executable protection. Inspect, inventory and measure passed using the installed audit package; these do not verify product behavior. Git and Node versions were captured by inspect.
limitations: Native product checks and real-product journey execution are unavailable because the application is absent. Language/outside research was not undertaken: this bounded checkpoint needs only repository evidence and proposes no external service or language-specific tooling. Main-thread research used because three files make delegation wasteful.
